notes: Use-case summary: primary product is an in-app financial advisor chat. Must be low-latency for 1:1 user conversations and fast re-ranking for search results.

Traffic profile (from customer traces): steady-state 50-70 QPS weekdays 09:00-18:00 PT; nightly batch embedding jobs spike token throughput; marketing-driven flash events (campaigns) produce short peaks up to ~320 QPS for 15-90 minutes.

Baseline sizing targets requested by customer: maintain <= 150ms p50 and <= 350ms p99 end-to-end for 512-token prompts at steady-state traffic; p99 can relax to 600ms during controlled bursts but customer prefers graceful degradation with fallback routing rather than failures.

Token throughput planning: steady-state tokens/sec target ~7.2k TPS (60 QPS * avg 120 tokens/response); peak tokens/sec observed ~38.4k TPS (320 QPS * 120 tokens). Customer expects Redwood to size reserved GPUs to hit steady-state SLA and provide clear headroom for burst handling via fallback models and vertical autoscale/burst buckets.

Model preferences: primary model = "Redwood-70B-chat-int8" (verified latency profile), fallback = "meta-13B-q4" for bursts and reranking. Customer is open to additional quantization (int4) if output quality checks pass. Want deterministic rollouts and pin-by-version for compliance.

Routing & fallback policy: require cross-region fallback to EU cluster only for disaster scenarios; prefer local NA Dedicated pool otherwise. Must support automatic fallback to 13B variant when latency SLOs are in danger or capacity exhausted.
SLA asks: 99.9% availability for reserved pool; target 99th percentile latency SLOs as above; credits for SLA misses; monthly performance report with token-level cost breakdown.

Networking/security: VPC peering + private endpoints required; strict egress rules, customer will provide peering CIDR and lists. KMS integration required for model payload encryption at rest. Full audit logs required for every inference call (request id + user id + model version).

POC ask: 2-week PoC on Dedicated pool using customer subset data and shadow traffic replay. Deliverables: observed p50/p95/p99 latency matrix, GPU utilization curves, recommended reserved GPU count, suggested autoscale thresholds and fallback rules.

Quote from CTO (call 2026-01-10): "We cannot afford >0.5s tail latency on our advisor flows — customers drop off. If you can show steady-state cost parity with our infra and a clean fallback for bursts, we'll move to a yearly reserved contract."

Redwood SE notes (2026-02-05): suggested starting point for reserved GPUs = 8 x H100-equivalent for steady-state (int8 70B baseline) with 4-slot burst pool for short peaks; final numbers to be validated in sizing workshop and synthetic load tests.
